findings.title: Final response permits informational status and omits the 205 no-content rule

evidence.observation: StatusCode/NoContent/NotFound validates100–599 and only204/304 suppress output; response_begin is a single final commit and Upgrade is unsupported.
Informational status precedes a final response and cannot carry content or trailers.

findings.impact: An accepted public status can fail to terminate the request correctly or allow protocol-invalid body framing.
findings.expected_fix: Define final response validation independently from informational handling; v1 should reject1xx through final status APIs, include205 body prohibition, and specify compatible HEAD/204/205/304 content-length/trailer behavior in managed/native validation.

resolution.summary: Sections5 and5.1 reject final1xx/out-of-range status in public and native admission; HEAD/204/205/304 each specify producer, trailer and Content-Length behavior, including HEAD combined with a stricter status.
resolution.scope: Independent review of the design repair; not runtime acceptance.

findings.title: HTTP header strings and decoded gRPC binary metadata lack distinct ABI projections

evidence.observation: request_info exposes one headers view while the gRPC metadata convention requires raw binary values for-bin and explicitly no ABI base64.
One public context exposes both ordinary HTTP HeaderCollection strings and typed gRPC text/binary metadata.

findings.impact: The current projection cannot unambiguously preserve HTTP wire header text and independently decoded binary gRPC values; one wrapper can incorrectly UTF8-decode raw binary or decode base64 twice.
findings.expected_fix: Define a separate exact typed ABI projection/field for gRPC metadata, including owner kind, lease, byte budget and whether wire HTTP headers remain intact; update C header/probe if layout changes.
findings.remaining_after_projection_fix: Separate metadata projection is now explicit and C header/probe agree. The remaining clause attributing comma-coalesced splitting to Tonic must instead identify bounded Adapter splitting before per-entry Tonic decode.

followup_evidence.observation: MetadataValue::to_bytes invokes VE::decode on the whole value.
Binary decode directly invokes the base64 decoder, without comma splitting.

findings.title: Trusted forwarded metadata has no deterministic parsing and trust contract

evidence.observation: Exact direct-peer addresses and a finite hop count are stated, but header names/precedence, hop traversal/trust, mismatched repeated lists, scheme/authority validation and MCP Host boundary are not fixed.

findings.impact: Different implementations can accept different client-supplied identity metadata or apply a forwarded authority to an unrelated Host allowlist.
findings.expected_fix: Define the supported forwarding header family, bounded right-to-left trusted-hop traversal, per-hop trust checks, invalid/duplicate/mismatched input behavior, effective Scheme/Host and original-peer preservation, and the authority used by MCP Host checks.

resolution.summary: Section4.4 fixes the exact supported X-Forwarded family, aligned bounded lists, strict IP/scheme/authority validation, right-to-left per-hop membership, atomic metadata update and original peer/Host/Origin preservation.
resolution.scope: Independent review of the design repair; not runtime acceptance.

findings.title: Completion or disposal failure can leave request retirement obligations unspecified

evidence.observation: OnStarting is LIFO and scope waits for callbacks/disposables, but OnCompleted/disposable ordering and behavior after one throws are not stated.

findings.impact: An implementation could skip later cleanup, omit dispatch_complete, leak the DI scope or leave Close pending forever after a user cleanup exception.
findings.expected_fix: Fix the ordering and exactly-once rules, isolate failures so remaining registered cleanup and scope disposal still run, retain the original/first error with bounded safe diagnostics, and always signal dispatch completion and join native retirement in the outer finally path.
findings.remaining_after_cleanup_fix: Failure-isolated LIFO callbacks/disposables/scope and outer dispatch completion now close cleanup. Still specify that successful MapRaw/direct-response dispatch automatically awaits HTTP CompleteAsync before cleanup when not already completed; otherwise the sample setting only StatusCode201 can leave response_finish absent.

findings.title: Unexecuted Stream result does not specify source ownership

evidence.observation: The source is disposed on completion/error unless leaveOpen, but construction versus execution transfer is undefined. A filter can replace a returned result before execution; ServerResult has no disposal contract.

findings.impact: The normal caller cannot determine who closes an already-open Stream when execution never starts or early validation/cancellation fails.
findings.expected_fix: Define exact transfer at execution admission or another implementable ownership seam; unexecuted results must retain caller ownership, or expose an actual deterministic release mechanism. Prefer a producer example that opens resources inside its awaited execution and guarantees closure on failure.

resolution.summary: Section5.2 makes successful single-use Execute admission the transfer point, with immediate finally installation and explicit unexecuted/failed-admission caller ownership; the new Download producer opens and closes its FileStream only during actual execution and compiles.
resolution.scope: Independent review of the design repair; not runtime acceptance.

findings.title: MCP pre-parse authentication and native automatic-method authorization have no ABI continuation

evidence.observation: B19 requires Host/Origin/auth before parse and lists/get/read/call share the authenticated policy.

The MCP exports take already-native-parsed arguments and submit replies; no explicit pre-auth route ticket and allow/deny resume operation admits the public rmcp service before its parser or automatic list handlers.

findings.impact: The current exact export inventory cannot demonstrate the required order for managed auth callbacks before native parsing; automatic list/metadata responses may bypass the application authorization path.
findings.expected_fix: Specify the outer native protocol request gate, bounded pre-auth ticket/context, asynchronous managed middleware/auth outside the callback, precise allow/deny continuation ABI, cancellation/failure cleanup, and subsequent business dispatch identity without duplicate request ownership. All protocol methods, including native automatic lists, must pass the gate.
findings.remaining_after_gate_fix: The explicit phased single-ticket MCP allow/deny gate and nested invocation lease now close pre-parse authorization. Still clarify all gRPC/MCP RequestContext body/response/OnStarting/filter restrictions, with typed protocol metadata/status as the only admitted output path after protocol admission.

findings.title: Metadata-view paragraph ambiguously claims ownership transfer

evidence.observation: After metadata_headers is declared to return a borrowed view, the same paragraph says this operation transfers an independently released metadata owner.

findings.impact: The intended bound_addresses owner transfer is easy to confuse with the borrowed metadata_headers projection.
findings.expected_fix: Name bound_addresses explicitly as the owner-returning operation and metadata_headers as a view-only borrow under that owner lease.

resolution.summary: Section10.2 names bound_addresses as the owner-transfer export; both header projections return lease-bound views, reject incompatible kinds and leave out views empty on failure.
resolution.scope: Independent review of the design repair; not runtime acceptance.

findings.title: Coverage rows do not identify their inspected-source evidence

evidence.observation: All65 feature rows list comparison APIs but lack per-row source IDs or exact reused native-evidence paths; the companion manifest gives scoped reads without a mechanically explicit feature mapping.

findings.impact: A future maintainer cannot distinguish source-supported comparisons from uninspected family members or locate the pinned native evidence for a row without inference.
findings.expected_fix: Map rows to actual SERVER-DOTNET/RUST source IDs and relevant reused native evidence, with explicit coverage limits where a named comparison member was not individually read; do not cite unread files or claim a whole-file read from a hash.

resolution.summary: All65 rows now resolve inspected-source IDs or exact reused source records and existing native evidence paths. Coverage limits distinguish family comparisons from individually inspected overloads and explicitly identify unsupported own-policy rows. The independent link check found no missing/unread referenced record.
resolution.scope: Independent review of the design repair; not runtime acceptance.

findings.title: MCP tool root-shape admissibility is ambiguous

evidence.observation: AddTool generics and supported schema forms include scalar/array/object shapes, while the exact argument bridge describes a registered input object and output structuredContent; root shape and null-root rejection are unstated.

findings.impact: A static codec alone could appear to authorize a scalar/array registration that the selected method/argument model does not bind.
findings.expected_fix: Declare and validate the selected root policy at registration. The author-selected v1 repair is a non-null object input and output root, with scalar/array/null allowed only at explicitly described nested properties, and actionable diagnostics.

resolution.summary: Section8 fixes finite non-null object roots and explicitly rejects Nullable<T>, scalar/array/dictionary/open/polymorphic roots. The reference-DTO root-only TransformSchemaNode narrows the erased top-level nullability without changing nested schemas. Reviewed BCL witness preserves its initial failure, final7 positive/5 rejection result and matching source/log hashes; no product execution is claimed.
resolution.scope: Independent review of the design repair; not runtime acceptance.

findings.title: Retained inbound native chunks can consume the response progress capacity

sections: 10.3 native write reservation and managed/native ordering
evidence.observation: Chunk may equal per-request cap; independent inbound owners can retain native credit across reads; positive output asynchronously waits for that same request/global native capacity. Only managed/native ordering, not same-side retained-owner progress, is fixed.
Each direction must have temporary chunk headroom and cyclic holding is prohibited, but the concrete API does not specify protected headroom/global admission or nonwaiting exhaustion.
Input buffers and output write reservations are distinct owners; starting a write does not transfer/release held input buffers.

counterexample: Use default Br=4MiB and K=32KiB, with the supported route body-limit override admitting at least4MiB.
Retain128 full BodyChunk owners, then await a positive Response.WriteAsync before finally disposing those chunks; output memory may already be application-owned.

Per-request native free credit is0. Only handler-owned chunk disposal can create space, while that handler awaits the write. Deadline/cancellation eventually ends the wait, but normal response progress cannot occur.
findings.impact: A currently admitted application pattern suffers a deadline-bounded liveness failure despite satisfying one-reader/one-writer and managed/native acquisition order. This is a static contract gap, not an executed product failure or a permanent unbounded deadlock.
findings.expected_fix: Select an exact protected per-direction/request headroom rule with validation and atomic global admission, or explicit nonwaiting resource_limit when held owners prevent progress. Apply to real backing capacities and both read/write exhaustion; add B16 boundary/global/cancellation witnesses. A per-request floor alone cannot guarantee global capacity.

limitations: No product Server exists in this phase. No HTTP/TLS/protocol execution, production budget proof, Windows certification or generated handler execution is inferred from declarations.
No acceptance binding or GitHub approval has been created. Exact-content recheck is required after fixes.
observations: Ordinary handlers, JSON DTOs, gRPC descriptors and MCP registrations reuse one maintainer-built Rust asset; no per-application Rust build path is required by the inspected declarations.
Control callback, sticky request cancellation snapshot, host-fault latch and request_try_retire make cancellation and dispatch-root retirement explicit; raw callbacks do not run application work.
Native write reservation -> nonwaiting managed credit -> bounded synchronous copy -> final-owner credit release is explicit, including never-started/failed-create rollback.
BoundAddresses has an actual startup metadata-owner path for port zero; request, metadata, body-chunk and operation ownership are separated.
Whole-call gRPC deadlines, four cardinalities, identity-only compression and distinct status/error layers are declared; no production protocol execution is inferred.
MCP parsing/schema allocation proof remains an explicit B19 gate; its current documents do not assert that wire size alone bounds JSON/DTO peak.

Getting Started and the Server section of guides use the same minimal/typed handler overloads as the compile-only consumer; static System.Text.Json generation is separated from the unimplemented endpoint generator.
